aspects.says: An abstract method added to a fat interface breaks every implementation, test fakes for clients that never call it included; a new role breaks nobody.
basis: section:A Method Added to a Fat Interface Breaks Classes That Never Call It

aspects.says: A client that only reads takes the reading role, so it runs on implementations that can't write.
basis: section:Role Interfaces Turn the Refusal into a Compile Error

aspects.says: A read-only implementation of a JDK collection interface, Java 21's SequencedCollection included, compiles calls to the mutators it offers and refuses them at run time, since no read-only role exists to implement instead.
basis: section:Collection Is Fat on Purpose, and Java 21's SequencedCollection Repeats It

aspects.says: An inherited default runs without the implementation's own rules, such as its lock, so a class with such rules overrides it.
basis: section:A Default Method Keeps Implementations Compiling, and Runs Code That Never Saw Their Locks

aspects.says: A default method lets implementations written before it compile and work unchanged.
basis: section:A Default Method Keeps Implementations Compiling, and Runs Code That Never Saw Their Locks

aspects.says: Splitting the interface into roles lets the read-only implementation drop its writer methods, so handing it to a client that writes no longer compiles.
basis: section:Role Interfaces Turn the Refusal into a Compile Error

aspects.says: A role is the set of methods one client uses together; one interface per method makes a client that needs several carry an intersection type.
basis: section:Split by Client, Not by Method

aspects.says: An implementation that throws UnsupportedOperationException from a method of a fat interface compiles, and the wiring mistake that calls it fails only at run time.
basis: section:A Fat Interface Compiles Calls Its Implementations Can Only Refuse
